question: Of the following pairs of surface molecules, what is used by the virgin T lymphocytes to extravasate to the lymph node?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Virgin T lymphocytes" -> "express L-selectin" -> "bind to high endothelial venules" -> "extravasate to lymph nodes" -> "CCR7 guides migration" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Virgin T lymphocytes" -> "require surface molecules for migration" -> "L-selectin facilitates adhesion" -> "CCR7 directs movement towards lymph nodes" -> 90%
CHAIN: "L-selectin" -> "mediates rolling on endothelium" -> "CCR7" -> "responds to chemokines" -> "promotes entry into lymph nodes" -> 92%
CHAIN: "CCR7 and L-selectin" -> "are critical for T cell trafficking" -> "allow virgin T lymphocytes to extravasate" -> "to lymph nodes" -> 93%
analysis: Virgin T lymphocytes express L-selectin, which helps them to bind to high endothelial venules (HEVs) in lymph nodes. Additionally, CCR7 is a chemokine receptor that guides T cells to the lymph nodes by responding to the chemokines CCL19 and CCL21 produced in the lymph nodes. Therefore, the correct pair of surface molecules used by virgin T lymphocytes to extravasate to the lymph node is CCR7 and L-selectin.
